rationale: The literature confirms that the primary discovery linking BRD4 mutations to a Cornelia de Lange-like syndrome (CdLS6) was published by Olley et al. in Nature Genetics under PMID 29379197 in 2018. Subsequent erratum/publisher correction notices (e.g., indexed separately in bibliographic records) serve as editorial amendments and author corrections to the original article, rather than independent primary clinical cohort studies.

evidence.text: The primary paper 'BRD4 interacts with NIPBL and BRD4 is mutated in a Cornelia de Lange-like syndrome' authored by G. The entry indicates that the primary clinical phenotype associated with BRD4 haploinsufficiency overlaps with Cornelia de Lange syndrome and notes an amendment link.

evidence.text: Lonardo (2025) reviews non-classic Cornelia de Lange syndrome due to BRD4 alterations, discussing atypical CdLS associated with BRD4 gene alterations and citing the foundational role of BRD4 variants in patient phenotypes.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 ...
source.quote: Pathogenic variations in the NIPBL gene account for the majority of cases, but variations in several other genes, including BRD4, have been identified as causative factors for non-classic or milder forms of the syndrome. This review aims to analyse the roles that BRD4 plays in the various pathways in which it is involved and to summarise current knowledge on atypical CdLS associated with BRD4 gene alterations

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact distinguishing phenotypic frequencies between classic NIPBL-associated CdLS and BRD4-associated CdLS6 in expanded cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: While CdLS6 shows phenotypic overlap with classic CdLS (such as developmental delay and facial dysmorphisms), characterization of non-classic or milder manifestations requires large cross-cohort meta-analyses.
